note: Bitmap font glyphs for the world-map march queue. Windows OCR reads this region as '115' for '1/5', so the runtime uses template matching. Digits 0, 2, 3 and 4 are not observed yet; the reader returns UNKNOWN_GLYPH for them rather than guessing.

calibration.why: threshold 200 sat on a cliff: one pixel of antialiasing shrank the / glyph from 3x10 to 2x8, so a real 1/5 on a live frame was refused as UNKNOWN_GLYPH
calibration.evidence: across 161 stored 1366x768 frames, READ went 14 -> 17 and UNKNOWN_GLYPH 7 -> 3; no frame that already READ changed its value, and every newly recovered read was verified by eye to be 1/5
calibration.glyph_shapes: 1 is 4x8, / is 3x10, 5 is 6x8 at this threshold, against 3x7 / 3x10 / 4x8 at 200
calibration.stability_check: at 160 and 180 the three glyphs segment identically on both the training frame and an independent live frame; at 200 and 220 they do not
